Ok, a few things:

1) Geiger counters measure ionizing radiation. Ionizing radiation can kill you (either quickly or slowly dependent on the dose). NO ONE uses equipment that emits ionizing radiation for communications because such high frequencies are absorbed by basically everything. That's why ionizing radiation such as xrays are used for medical imaging - it's so easily obstructed that high power usage from inches away can barely penetrate bones.

2) Cellular communications exclusively use non-ionizing radiation sprinkled across the 600mhz - 6ghz bands (different carriers have different frequencies licensed from the FCC or local equivalent). This radiation can only harm you if the power level is dramatically higher than cell towers are capable of putting out (the transmitters and antennas have strict limitations on their EIRP that the FCC enforces in a "$50k fine per antenna per day because fuck you" manner). This damage would manifest as a extremely unsubtle physical heating effect. As in, literally what your microwave does. The difference is that your typical kitchen microwave outputs 600-1200 watts. 5g cell towers top out at around 20 watts if you're literally hanging off the tower - and that degrades rapidly with distance. Your phone outputs a couple watts. For perspective, the lightbulb in your refridgerator is around 30-40 watts and isnt doing eff all to harm you because the wattage is literally too low.

3) The only outdoor transmitters in the 600mhz - 6ghz range that output enough power to cause burns are some large weather radar implementations that are fenced, raised off the ground, and pointed up into the sky to keep idiots from trying to cook hotdogs in front of them.

Source: I used to be an RF Engineer and needed to know this to climb telecom towers safely (e.g. "If I grab that antenna over yonder is the NOC going to bitch at me for degrading the signal or will it burn me?"). Everything used for cellular communications is in former category. The only risk cell towers pose to you is if a tornado knocks one over and crushes you.
